title: Metric watermark sidecar for exactly-once inference KPI delivery
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Inference KPI streams suffer duplicate or missing per-request metrics when requests are retried, rerouted, or when collectors/aggregators restart. This makes SLO calculation and attribution noisy and causes billing inaccuracies for Dedicated customers. Existing heuristics (trace ID matching, timestamp bucketing) are brittle under network reordering and batching.

Proposal: Implement a 'metric watermark' sidecar deployed with inference workers that emits a lightweight deterministic watermark token with every metric and exemplar. The watermark provides a compact, monotonic per-request namespace (tenant + request fingerprint + sequence) that lets downstream collectors perform robust exactly-once deduplication and deterministic reassembly across batching/resharding windows.

Core features: 
- Watermark generation: stable 128-bit token derived from (tenant_id, request_id, short fingerprint of prompt/hash, per-request monotonic seq for multi-span emissions).
- Distributed eviction: sidecar exposes watermark lifetime hints to aggregator via resource attribute rw_watermark_ttl to bound dedupe state.
- Transport: add rw_watermark (hex) + rw_seq + rw_req_phase labels to OTLP metric Resource/Exemplar and Prometheus labels/exemplars. For systems that don't support labels, attach watermark as OTLP resource attribute.
- Backwards compatibility: when downstream doesn't support watermark-based dedupe, aggregator falls back to existing trace-link heuristics. Sidecar has a 'compat' mode where it mirrors previous telemetry labels to avoid schema breakage.
- Performance targets: CPU overhead <1% p50 for 4k QPS workload, additional p95 latency added <2ms on x86 inference node, memory <8MB.
- Observability: instrumentation for sidecar health, watermark collision rate, dedupe reductions, and watermark TTL evictions.

Design trade-offs: 
- Deterministic vs random token: choose deterministic derived token to enable idempotent dedupe across retries from different nodes. Adds requirement that request inputs used for fingerprinting must be stable (we accept tiny probability of collision).
- Storage vs TTL: longer TTL increases dedupe accuracy but raises memory. We'll expose a per-tenant config with sensible defaults (60s for high-throughput customers, 5s for low-latency).
- Label cardinality: adding rw_watermark increases cardinality for some metric sets. We mitigate by only exposing watermark on exemplars and a small set of per-request metrics; other aggregate metrics will carry only a watermark-bucket tag (low-cardinality).

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline: sidecar -> OTLP collector -> aggregator -> Prometheus remote-write shows >=95% reduction in duplicates on synthetic retry-heavy workload vs baseline heuristics.
- No regressions: CPU and latency stay within performance targets for p50/p95 under our CI workload.
- Feature flagged rollout: can enable watermark per-tenant without requiring downstream changes.
- Production canary: 2% traffic for 24h with detailed dashboard (collision rate, dedupe ratio, memory pressure) before ramp.

Rollout plan:
1) Library + local sidecar prototype with unit tests and perf harness (ENG-430210, ENG-430211)
2) Integrate with OTLP collector adapter and add exemplar label support in aggregator (backend PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pulls/1823)
3) Canary on staging tenants, gather metrics, iterate on TTL and label exposure
4) GA with tenant opt-in and console flagging (telemetry-2025.04 release)

acceptance_criteria: Sidecar successfully annotates OTLP/Prometheus metrics with rw_watermark and rw_seq without schema-breaking changes for non-adopting stacks
End-to-end duplicate rate reduced >=95% on synthetic retry workload compared to baseline
Sidecar overhead within performance targets: CPU <1% p50, added latency <2ms p95, memory <8MB
Canary deployment shows stable memory and no increase in metric cardinality for aggregate dashboards
Dashboards and alerts created: watermark_collision_rate > 0.1% alert, dedupe_ratio < 50% alert
